purpose: SEC-DB-RLS-001 I1: the target database identity model. Explicit grants, no default privileges: a table that is not listed here gets no runtime access (fails closed) and the verifier fails CI until it is classified. Nothing in this file is applied to production by I1.

identities.vexa_migrator: owns every object in the public schema and runs migrations (deploy time only); NOSUPERUSER, BYPASSRLS because tables are FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY and data-fixing migrations must see every tenant; an owner can disable RLS regardless, so this adds no isolation risk; never held by the runtime path
identities.vexa_runtime: the API; table-level privileges from runtime.tables; owns nothing; no DDL; NOSUPERUSER NOBYPASSRLS
identities.vexa_backup: read-only; BYPASSRLS is its only extra attribute, justified solely because pg_dump must read forced-RLS tables; SELECT only
identities.vexa_ops: operator path for the platform control tables only (the kill switch and the platform budget periods)

noCrossTenantMaintenanceRole: Deliberately not provisioned. Known cross-tenant jobs use tenant iteration, or a SELECT-only maintenance policy on specific tables (see docs/qa/sec-db-rls-001-call-site-classification-2026-10-06.md). A maintenance role is added only when a named job needs it and cannot iterate.

exceptionsToCrud.ai_platform_controls: SELECT only: operators write the kill switch through vexa_ops, never the API
exceptionsToCrud.ai_platform_budget_periods: SELECT and UPDATE only: the API moves counters, operators create and delete periods
